newsitem.title: CANADA: Cominco sees '97 refined zinc output down.
newsitem.headline: Cominco sees '97 refined zinc output down.

text.p: Cominco Ltd, the world's largest zinc miner, said on Thursday it expected to produce 370,000 tonnes of refined zinc in 1997, down slightly from 377,300 tonnes in 1996.

The company forecast it would increase refined zinc output by 40,000 tonnes in 1998 from production facilities under construction in Trail, British Columbia and Cajamarquilla in Peru, Cominco Chief Executive David Thompson told the annual meeting.
If Cominco further expanded its Cajamarquilla operation, it would have the capacity to produce 500,000 tonnes of refined zinc by 2000, Thompson said.

Cominco expected to produce 550,000 tonnes of zinc contained in concentrate in 1997 and should boost output to 740,000 tonnes by 1999, due to a production increase under way at its Red Dog facility in Alaska, Thompson said.
He said Cominco budgeted $190 million for capital expenditures and $40 million for exploration in 1997.
